security_spec.violation_condition: In XiangShan RTL, the indirect CSR access logic (Smcsrind/Sscsrind) fails when: (1) miselect/siselect/vsiselect WARL masking is incomplete, allowing illegal select values to be retained and subsequently used as indices into mireg*/sireg*/vsireg* alias windows, causing access to unmapped or cross-privilege-level register state; (2) the mstateen0[60] / hstateen0[60] access-control gating is missing or bypassable, permitting S-mode or VS-mode code to access siselect/sireg*/vsiselect/vsireg* when the state-enable bit is cleared; (3) the virtual-instruction exception logic for VS/VU-mode direct access to vsiselect/vsireg* or VU-mode access to siselect/sireg* is absent or misrouted, allowing guest code to directly manipulate hypervisor-controlled indirect CSR windows; (4) the MSB-based custom-vs-standard address-space partitioning (bit XLEN-1) is not enforced in decode, causing custom select values to alias into standard-allocated ranges or vice versa; (5) the siselect/sireg* and vsiselect/vsireg* register widths are hardcoded to SXLEN/VSXLEN instead of tracking current XLEN, causing truncation or zero-extension mismatches during M-mode access on XLEN-mismatched harts (e.g., MXLEN=64, SXLEN=32); (6) the mireg* CSR number gap (miph at 0x354) is not respected in the CSR decode module, causing mireg4/mireg5/mireg6 to alias with miph or adjacent CSRs.
security_spec.summary: Indirect CSR access (Smcsrind/Sscsrind) introduces a new CSR windowing mechanism where WARL-masked select registers index into alias register arrays; incorrect RTL implementation of WARL masking, state-enable access control (mstateen0/hstateen0 bit 60), virtual-instruction fault gating, MSB address-space partitioning, XLEN width tracking, or CSR number decode gap (miph at 0x354) can cause privilege escalation by allowing lower-privilege code to read/write register state through the indirect window that should be inaccessible.
